definition: The integrated discipline of aligning IT and business objectives (governance), identifying and treating uncertainty (risk), and meeting legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations (compliance). In an audit context, GRC frameworks structure how controls are selected, tested, and reported.

The international standard for establishing, operating, and certifying an Information Security Management System (ISMS). The 2022 revision organizes 93 Annex A controls into four themes: Organizational, People, Physical, and Technological.

A voluntary framework from the US National Institute of Standards and Technology organized into six functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover. Auditors use its categories and subcategories to benchmark an organization's cybersecurity posture.

Authentication requiring two or more independent factors: knowledge (password), possession (token, device), or inherence (biometric). Auditors test MFA coverage on remote access, privileged accounts, and cloud consoles — gaps here are consistently high-severity findings.

The ISO 27001 document that lists every Annex A control, states whether it applies to the organization, and justifies inclusions and exclusions. It is the anchor artifact of any ISO 27001 audit — certification bodies review it first.
